096.t: Primary Storage: RAM, ROM and Cache
o: Recall key facts about primary storage: ram, rom and cache.
Work through a new example with correct technical language.
Apply the method independently and justify your answer.
c: RAM stores programs and data currently in use. It is volatile: its contents are lost when power is removed.
ROM is non-volatile and typically stores essential firmware or startup instructions.
Cache is small, very fast memory close to the processor, holding frequently or recently used data and instructions.
RAM is general working memory; ROM retains firmware; cache reduces repeated slower memory accesses.

m.title: Primary Storage: RAM, ROM and Cache · worked example
m.q: A laptop uses RAM, ROM and cache. Explain the role of each and why cache helps the CPU. [6 marks]
st: RAM stores active programs/data; ROM retains firmware across shutdown.
Cache holds frequently used instructions/data close to CPU, reducing RAM access.
RAM and cache are volatile; ROM retains contents without power. [2 marks for each correctly explained role]

w: Explain why opening more applications increases demand for RAM. [4]
Each open program requires instructions/data in RAM [1]. More active applications occupy more RAM [1]. Available RAM decreases [1], potentially requiring virtual memory [1].
A device must retain startup code when unplugged. Explain why ROM is suitable. [4]
ROM retains its contents without power [1], so firmware remains available after shutdown [1]. Startup instructions can be accessed when switched on [1], allowing the device to initialise [1].
Explain why CPU cache is usually smaller than RAM but helps performance. [4]
Cache provides faster access than RAM [1] for frequently needed data [1], reducing time waiting for memory [1]. It is more expensive per unit of storage, so is generally smaller [1].

k.q: Predict which message appears if free RAM is 900 MB.
k.code:
freeMB = 900
neededMB = 700
if freeMB >= neededMB then
    print("Load")
else
    print("Wait")
endif
p: Change neededMB to 950 and predict again.
Change the comparison to > and test the equality case.
k.a: Load; after changing neededMB to 950 it prints Wait. With > and equal values, it prints Wait.
